description: The infrared channel of Hubble’s Wide Field Camera 3 covers approximately 800–1700 nm. It provides 15 broad-, medium- and narrow-band imaging filters and the G102 and G141 grisms.
facility_description: The NASA/ESA Hubble Space Telescope is a 2.4-m reflecting telescope operating in low-Earth orbit.
notes: Researched 2026-10-26. Licence classification applies to STScI-produced, unmarked calibration data under the STScI content use policy, which separately requests NASA/STScI acknowledgement. Separately copyrighted third-party material is excluded. Do not redistribute the cited papers themselves under this data policy. Original source family is STScI synphot component tables; the owner throughput documentation explains total-system response. Existing NJM curves were not downloaded, hash-matched, replaced or assigned a new calibration epoch in this research. No DetectorType changes. The HST acknowledgement is copied verbatim as a conditional publication template, including its unfilled program placeholder. No grant acknowledgement is claimed. Calamida et al. (2022) characterises the calibration of all 42 full-frame UVIS filters, 20 quad filters and 15 IR imaging filters. G280, G102 and G141 are excluded from these imaging-filter references. The owner throughput appendix defines response in detected electrons relative to incident photons, and notes the ultraviolet quantum-yield caveat. UVIS1 and UVIS2 calibrations are chip dependent. No single magnitude system is asserted: multiple systems are supported.
